properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 953016 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: GRANT MACKAY
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 953016
Incident Time: 2010-08-31 15:00:00
Nearest City: Houston, TX
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: GRANT MACKAY
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 40 gallons
DURING DEMO ON OUR CONSTRUCTION SITE A TRUCK PUNCTURED ONE OF THE SADDLE FUEL TANKS SPILLING APPROX. 20-40 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL ONTO A PAVED SURFACE ON OUR JOB-SITE. THE TRUCK WAS IN THE PROCESS OF HAULING OFF CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS WHEN IT RAN OVER A PIECE OF DEBRIS CAUSING THE PUNCTURE IN THE FUEL TANK. THIS WAS NOTICED IMMEDIATELY AND WE WERE ABLE TO CONTAIN THE LEAKING FUEL WITH SOIL, ISOLATING THE FUEL TO THE IMMEDIATE AREA AND PREVENTING ANY FUEL FROM REACHING A STORM DRAIN INLET. WE THEN PUT DOWN A HIGH ABSORBENT MATERIAL TO SOAK UP THE FUEL. ONCE THIS WAS DONE WE BAGGED ALL CONTAMINATED MATERIAL AND HAULED IT OFF SITE TO DISPOSE OF PROPERLY. ALL CONTAMINATED MATERIAL HAS BEEN CLEANED UP AND PROPERLY DISPOSED OF.

properties.title: NRC Report: Isopar M Kerosene in Sea Surface near New Orleans, LA
properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 883663 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: WESTERNGECO
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 883663
Incident Time: 2008-09-09 20:30:00
Nearest City: New Orleans, LA
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: ISOPAR M KEROSENE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: WESTERNGECO
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 328.08 feet by 164.04 feet (area 1.24 acres)
Reported Spill Volume: 39.63 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 1.32 gallons
NEPTUNE WAS PROCEEDING SOUTH WEST AWAY FROM HURRICANE IKE, PLANNING TO BRING ON THE TWO INNER STREAMERS OF A TEN STREAMER JOB. THE SEPARATION ROPE BETWEEN 4 & 5 WAS TAKEN OFF FROM STREAMER 5 AND PUT ON THE LEAD-IN OF 4. STREAMER 4 WAS THEN REDEPLOYED. AT 20:30Z STREAMER 5 SPIKED WITH TENSION AND APPEARED TO SNAP. POSITION WAS 26 15.6N, 90 57.7W. SPEED WAS REDUCED. TAILBUOY 5 STILL SEEMED TO BE FOLLOWING SPREAD CORRECTLY. WORKBOAT WAS LAUNCHED TO INVESTIGATE IF STREAMER 5 WAS CAUGHT ON TAILBUOY 6, WHICH WAS CLOSE TO STERN. THIS WAS NOT THE CASE SO 6 WAS BROUGHT IN THE REST OF THE WAY. MOB BOAT WAS LAUNCHED TO PUT NORWEGIAN BUOY, WITH 50M OF STRONG ROPE, SHACKLED TO THE STRONG POINT ON THE TAILBUOY - THIS IN CASE THE STREAMER WENT LOOSE AND THE CHASEBOAT HAD TO TOW. STARBOARD STREAMERS BROUGHT FORWARD AND IT WAS SEEN THE SEPARATION ROPE WAS TOWING STREAMER 5. WORKBOAT WAS SENT OUT TO PUT A CLAMP ON THE FRONT END AND A ROPE WITH HOOK WAS FLOATED OUT FOR ATTACHMENT. STREAMER 5 WAS THEN BROUGHT TO THE GUN DECK (01:00Z ON 10TH). TWO SECTIONS WERE BADLY DAMAGED (BEYOND REPAIR) WITH LOSS OF KEROSENE INTO THE SEA. TIME LOSS WAS NOT RELEVANT AS IT IS WEATHER DOWNTIME TO AVOID HURRICANE IKE. IT IS THOUGHT THAT THE SEPARATION ROPE WAS EITHER LOOPED, OR GOT LOOPED, AROUND STREAMER 5 AS STREAMER 4 WAS BEING LET OUT. THIS LOOP EVENTUALLY CHOKED AND SNAPPED STREAMER 5.

POSITION WAS 26 15.6N, 90 57.7W. SPEED WAS REDUCED. TAILBUOY 5 STILL SEEMED TO BE FOLLOWING SPREAD CORRECTLY. WORKBOAT WAS LAUNCHED TO INVESTIGATE IF STREAMER 5 WAS CAUGHT ON TAILBUOY 6, WHICH WAS CLOSE TO STERN. THIS WAS NOT THE CASE SO 6 WAS BROUGHT IN THE REST OF THE WAY. MOB BOAT WAS LAUNCHED TO PUT NORWEGIAN BUOY, WITH 50M OF STRONG ROPE, SHACKLED TO THE STRONG POINT ON THE TAILBUOY - THIS IN CASE THE STREAMER WENT LOOSE AND THE CHASEBOAT HAD TO TOW. STARBOARD STREAMERS BROUGHT FORWARD AND IT WAS SEEN THE SEPARATION ROPE WAS TOWING STREAMER 5. WORKBOAT WAS SENT OUT TO PUT A CLAMP ON THE FRONT END AND A ROPE WITH HOOK WAS FLOATED OUT FOR ATTACHMENT. STREAMER 5 WAS THEN BROUGHT TO THE GUN DECK (01:00Z ON 10TH). TWO SECTIONS WERE BADLY DAMAGED (BEYOND REPAIR) WITH LOSS OF KEROSENE INTO THE SEA. TIME LOSS WAS NOT RELEVANT AS IT IS WEATHER DOWNTIME TO AVOID HURRICANE IKE. IT IS THOUGHT THAT THE SEPARATION ROPE WAS EITHER LOOPED, OR GOT LOOPED, AROUND STREAMER 5 AS STREAMER 4 WAS BEING LET OUT. THIS LOOP EVENTUALLY CHOKED AND SNAPPED STREAMER 5.

ON SATURDAY 12 OF DECEMBER AT APPROX. 3:00 PM THE FIRE ALARM SOUNDED IN THE GUARD HOUSE ADVISING AN ISSUE IN THE FIRE PUMP. THE SECURITY SHOWED UP TO INSPECT THE ROOM BUT HE FOUND EVERYTHING NORMAL IN THE AREA. AT 6:25 PM ANOTHER ALARM SOUNDED FROM THE PUMP HOUSE THE SECURITY GUARD RESPONDED AND THIS TIME THE SPRINKLER PUMP WAS RUNNING AND THE SPRINKLER HEAD ABOVE THE PUMP HAD GONE OFF. THE SECURITY GUARD CONTACT FACILITIES REPRESENTATIVE THAT SHOWED UP AT 7:06 PM AND IDENTIFIED THAT THE PUMP HAD BURN OUT ELECTRICAL DUE TO THE SPRINKLER GOING OFF. AFTER VERIFICATION TO THE SITE THEY PROCEED TO INSTALL ABSORBENT PADS TO CONTAIN THE SPILL. TODAY A BRIGADE SHOWED UP TO THE SITE TO CONDUCT A VISUAL INSPECTION AND PROCEED WITH THE CLEANING ACTIVITY TO THE SITE.

OTHER HOUSEHOLD RESIDENTS EXPERIENCE SIMILAR SYMPTOMS. THE CALLER'S PET WAS DIAGNOSED WITH A TUMOR, RESULTING IN DEATH, WHICH THE CALLER FEELS IS RELATED TO THE RELEASE OF PESTICIDES. CALLER REPORTS THE RELEASE OCCURS MULTIPLE TIMES A DAY EVERY SINGLE DAY.

Report Description/// THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT # 1452763 /// UPDATES: - INCIDENT LOCATION - TANK CAPACITY ADJUSTED FROM 1000 GALLONS TO 565 GALLONS - SPILL SIZE ADJUSTED FROM 565 GALLONS TO 60 GALLONS ORIGINAL REPORT: CALLER REPORTED THAT WHILE THE SUSPECTED RESPONSIBLE PARTY WAS DIGGING FOR CONSTRUCTION, AN UNDERGROUND TANK WAS STRUCK. AN ESTIMATED 450-500 GALLONS RELEASED FROM THE TANK TO SOIL BEFORE IT STOPPED LEAKING (AFTER THE CONTAINED MATERIAL WENT BELOW THE POINT OF IMPACT). THE TANK HAS A 1,000 GALLON CAPACITY AND IT WAS BELIEVED TO BE FULL PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT. NO DRAINS OR WATERWAYS WERE IMPACTED. IT IS UNKNOWN WHAT TYPE OF OIL RELEASED BUT THE CALLER STATED THAT THE LAND PREVIOUSLY WAS USED FOR FARMING AND IT MAY HAVE CONTAINED FUEL OR WASTE OIL. CALLER REPORTED THAT THE INCIDENT OCCURRED ON MONDAY 1/11 AT A TIME UNKNOWN TO THEM AND THE CALLER WAS NOT AWARE OF THE INCIDENT UNTIL IT WAS PUBLISHED IN THE LOCAL PAPER. THE CALLER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE INCIDENT ON 1/13 AT APPROX. 1900. /// THIS IS AN UPDATE TO NRC REPORT # 1452763 ///
